item.title: Teen hitman guilty of U.K. murder plot for Swedish crime group with Iran links
item.description: A 19-year-old Norwegian hitman was found guilty of an assassination plot after sending selfies with weapons to his girlfriend and friends.

item.title: Bloody, bare footprints lead to decadeslong search for woman's killer
item.description: In 1993, Jeanie Childs was found stabbed more than 60 times in her Minneapolis apartment. Bloody footprints and unknown DNA left investigators without answers until a 2015 cold-case review and public DNA database finally pointed to a suspect.

item.title: Watch: Fauci claims Paul has "unhinged obsession" with him, invokes Fifth Amendment at COVID hearing
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci delivered a brief opening statement at a Senate panel hearing on the origins of COVID-19, where Kentucky Republican Sen. Rand Paul demanded more answers about his involvement during the 2020 pandemic. Fauci accused Paul of having an "unhinged obsession" with him following years of public sparring.

item.title: Rare clue at Minneapolis crime scene points to a barefoot killer
item.description: "In Minnesota here, people are not committing crimes a lot of times with the socks and shoes off," said a forensic scientist about footprints left in the victim's blood.

item.title: Live Updates: Lindsay Clancy trial resumes with ex-husbands 911 call
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is standing trial on charges that she murdered her three young children in Duxbury, Massachusetts in 2023. Follow along for live updates on the second day of witness testimony.

item.title: 2 firefighters die in Greece as others fight massive blaze in France
item.description: Two firefighters died in a blaze on the Greek island of Crete Wednesday while crews in France confronted a wildfire four times the size of Paris, officials said.

item.title: Sneak peek: Death at Soho House
item.description: ENCORE: Did the son of an Oscar-winning songwriter strangle his swimsuit designer girlfriend in a chic New York City hotel or was her death an accident? "48 Hours" correspondent Troy Roberts reports Saturday, August 1 at 10/9c on CBS and streaming on Paramount+.

item.title: New chapter in Iran war after Saudi Arabia joins U.S. in attacks on Iran-backed proxies in Iraq
item.description: Four days of relative calm in the Iran war were shattered as the U.S. and Saudi Arabia joined forces to strike Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Also, the U.S. stopped Iran's "surprise attack" on a U.S. base in Jordan. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more information.

item.title: Fauci invokes 5th in hearing, citing Rand Paul's "unhinged obsession"
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci appeared before the Senate to testify on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic but invoked his Fifth Amendment rights in answering all questions.

item.title: Torrential rain causes major flooding in parts of the Northeast
item.description: Parts of New Jersey got up to 5 inches of rain on Tuesday as first responders pulled people out of flooded streets. In eastern Pennsylvania, heavy rain also flooded highways and roads. Rob Marciano reports.

item.title: Trump warns Iran is set to "get a beating" as 5-month war expands
item.description: The war in the Middle East is expanding, with Trump threatening Iran with "a beating" and the U.S. and Saudi Arabia jointly strike Iranian proxies in Iraq.

item.title: Federal Reserve weighs interest rate increase amid inflation, oil price whiplash
item.description: The Federal Reserve is set to consider whether to raise interest rates amid stubborn inflation pressures and oil price volatility. CBS News contributor J.D. Durkin has more.

item.title: Will the Federal Reserve increase interest rates?
item.description: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, but some believe inflation warrants a rate hike. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady has more.

item.title: Rand Paul removes Fauci's lawyer from COVID-19 pandemic hearing
item.description: Former top infectious disease expert Dr. Anthony Fauci is testifying before the Senate Homeland Security Committee on the COVID-19 pandemic. Dr. Fauci served under both the Trump and Biden administrations. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns and legal contributor Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: Key takeaways from Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary debate
item.description: Democratic gubernatorial hopefuls in Wisconsin took the stage Tuesday for a debate ahead of next week's primary. CBS News' Taurean Small has more.

item.title: The U.S. thwarted a surprise attack by Iran, CENTCOM says
item.description: CBS News' national security analyst Aaron MacLean joins to discuss overnight strikes in the Middle East after the U.S. says it thwarted a surprise missile attack by Iran.

item.title: Actor Jared Leto accused of criminal sexual conduct by 4 women
item.description: Four women say Hollywood star Jared Leto committed sexual crimes against them when they were teenagers, in interviews with the BBC.

item.title: Watch: Fauci invokes 5th Amendment in Senate hearing on COVID origins
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment during a Senate Homeland Security Committee hearing on the origins of COVID-19 days after Sen. Rand Paul released Fauci's diary entries from the pandemic. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has more.

item.title: Trump policy clears way for civil commitment of homeless in some states
item.description: In the year since President Trump signed an executive order aimed at moving homeless people off the streets, states have expanded involuntary treatment for the homeless.

item.title: Fauci to testify before Senate panel on COVID-19 origins, 6 years after start of pandemic
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci will appear in front of a Senate committee on Wednesday to answer questions about the origin and handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. It comes just days after Sen. Rand Paul released a trove of Fauci's diary entries in which he details his relationship with President Trump, the response to the pandemic and more.

item.title: What type of insurance you need to protect your home if a natural disaster strikes
item.description: Last year, the cost of damage from natural disasters in the U.S. was $115 billion. CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger explains what you need to know about insurance for your home, whether you own or rent.

item.title: Can hospitals still send unpaid medical bills to collections?
item.description: Worried an unpaid medical bill could follow you for years on end? Here's what to know about the collection rules.

item.title: Wisconsin Democrats debate policing, taxes, school vouchers in gubernatorial primary race
item.description: Wisconsin Democrats competing for the nomination in the governor's race debated the role of law enforcement after Madison police shot and killed a Black man during a botched arrest a week prior. CBS News' Taurean Small has more details.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: This family has been making wine for 6 centuries | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: From 2008, Morley Safer reports on an Italian family who's been making wine for six centuries, spanning the legendary vineyards of Tuscany and Umbria to their property in California's Napa Valley.

item.title: Singer-songwriter Glen Hansard killed in motorcycle crash
item.description: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard has died in a motorcycle crash.

item.title: Schools are testing pepper-spraying drones to stop shooters
item.description: Schools in three states will be equipped with drones this coming academic year that aim to find and deter active shooters within seconds.

item.title: Americans face higher back-to-school costs. Here's what's pricier.
item.description: U.S. households will spend roughly $4,000 per student on school supplies and lunches this year, a new analysis found.

item.title: Apalachee High School shooter sentenced to life without parole
item.description: Colt Gray, the teenager who admitted to killing four people in the 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School, will spend the rest of his life in prison without parole.

item.title: DOJ tests limits of never-before-used court to deport suspected terrorist
item.description: The Alien Terrorist Removal Court was created by Congress in 1996 and signed into law by President Bill Clinton. Before now, it had never been used.
